domain: California contractor license classifications and licensing requirements (CSLB): A / B / B-2 / C scope limits, asbestos and hazardous-substance certification, examinations and waivers, qualifying individuals, contractor / qualifier / LLC / disciplinary / judgment bonds, LLC liability insurance, reporting duties, license cancellation and inactive status, change-of-record notices, and CSLB arbitration
source_doc: 2026 CSLB California Contractors License Law & Reference Book (official), Section VI, B&P Code Article 4 'Classifications' (7054.5-7059.1), Article 5 'Licensing' (7065-7077), Article 6 'Records' (7080.5-7083.2) and the start of Article 6.2 'Arbitration' (7085-7085.5), PDF pages 270-326; file chunk lawbook_p271-325.txt

rules.title: Satellite antenna installers registered under B&P 9800 exempt
rules.plain_english: A person registered under the electronic and appliance repair dealer law (B&P 9800 et seq.) does not need a contractor license if all they do is install satellite antenna systems on homes or residential property.

parameters.exempt_activity: installing satellite antenna systems on residential structures or property only

rules.applies_to: Satellite antenna installers working on residential property
rules.verbatim_quote: The licensing provisions of this chapter do not apply to any person registered under Chapter 20 (commencing with Section 9800) if that person’s activities consist only of installing satellite antenna systems on residential structures or property.
rules.notes: Exemption is lost if the person does any other construction work. Commercial structures are not covered.

rules.title: Four branches of contracting: A, B, B-2, C
rules.plain_english: For licensing, California contracting is split into general engineering (A), general building (B), residential remodeling (B-2) and specialty (C) contracting. Every license classification falls into one of these branches.
rules.verbatim_quote: For the purpose of classification, the contracting business includes any or all of the following branches: (a) General engineering contracting. (b) (1) General building contracting. (2) Residential remodeling contracting. (c) Specialty contracting.
rules.notes: The B-2 code appears in 7057.5(d). The letter codes A, B and C are standard CSLB usage from the regulations (16 CCR), not stated in this section.

rules.title: General engineering contractor (A) scope
rules.plain_english: A general engineering contractor's main business is fixed works that need specialized engineering knowledge, such as roads, bridges, pipelines, sewers, dams, utilities, grading, paving and related concrete work.

fixed_works_examples: sewers and sewage disposal plants and systems
bridges, overpasses, underpasses and similar works
pipelines for petroleum and other liquid or gaseous substances
parks, playgrounds and other recreational works
refineries, chemical plants and similar industrial plants
powerhouses, powerplants and other utility plants and installations
excavating, grading, trenching, paving and surfacing
cement and concrete works in connection with the above fixed works

rules.applies_to: Contractors holding or seeking the A classification; owners choosing a contractor for engineering works
rules.verbatim_quote: A general engineering contractor is a contractor whose principal contracting business is in connection with fixed works requiring specialized engineering knowledge and skill, including the following divisions or subjects: irrigation, drainage, water power, water supply, flood control, inland waterways, harbors, docks and wharves, shipyards and ports, dams and hydroelectric projects
rules.notes: Excavating, grading, trenching, paving and concrete fall in A scope only when connected with the listed fixed works.

rules.title: General building contractor (B) definition: two or more unrelated trades
rules.plain_english: A general building contractor builds or superintends structures for sheltering people, animals or property, where the work uses at least two unrelated building trades. Someone who only supplies materials without installing them is not a B contractor.

parameters.structure_purpose: support, shelter, and enclosure of persons, animals, chattels, or movable property
parameters.excludes: material suppliers under B&P 7045 who do not fabricate or install the materials

rules.verbatim_quote: a general building contractor is a contractor whose principal contracting business is in connection with any structure built, being built, or to be built, for the support, shelter, and enclosure of persons, animals, chattels, or movable property of any kind, requiring in its construction the use of at least two unrelated building trades or crafts,

rules.title: B contractor prime contracts need 2+ unrelated trades besides framing/carpentry
rules.plain_english: A B contractor may take a prime contract for framing or carpentry alone. For any other prime contract, the job must involve at least two unrelated trades other than framing and carpentry, unless the B contractor holds the specialty license for the work or subcontracts it to a properly licensed contractor.

alternatives_if_below_minimum: B contractor holds the appropriate specialty classification
B contractor subcontracts the work to an appropriately licensed contractor

rules.applies_to: B general building contractors taking prime contracts
rules.verbatim_quote: a general building contractor shall not take a prime contract for any project involving trades other than framing or carpentry unless the prime contract requires at least two unrelated building trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry, or unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification or subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor
rules.notes: Check: count distinct unrelated trades in the contract scope, excluding framing and carpentry; if fewer than 2, require a matching specialty license or a licensed subcontractor for each trade.

verification.note: Prime-contract two-trade test, framing/carpentry exclusion and both cures (own classification or licensed sub) match. AB 433 effective 1/1/2014 matches history note.

rules.title: B contractor subcontracts need 2+ unrelated trades or the specialty license
rules.plain_english: A B contractor may take a subcontract for framing or carpentry. For any other subcontract, the subcontract must involve at least two unrelated trades other than framing and carpentry, or the B contractor must hold the specialty license itself. Sub-subcontracting does not cure this.

alternatives_if_below_minimum: B contractor holds the appropriate specialty classification

rules.applies_to: B general building contractors taking subcontracts
rules.verbatim_quote: A general building contractor shall not take a subcontract involving trades other than framing or carpentry, unless the subcontract requires at least two unrelated trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry, or unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification.
rules.notes: Unlike the prime-contract rule, the subcontract rule offers no option to pass the work to another licensed subcontractor.

verification.note: Subcontract test offers only 'holds the appropriate license classification'; no subcontract-out cure, as the rule says.

rules.title: B contractor may not contract fire protection or C-57 well drilling without license or licensed sub
rules.plain_english: A B contractor cannot contract for a project that includes a fire protection system or C-57 well drilling unless it holds that classification or subcontracts that work to a contractor who does.
rules.verbatim_quote: A general building contractor shall not contract for any project that includes a fire protection system as provided for in Section 7026.12 or 7026.13, or the “C-57” Well Drilling classification as provided for in Section 13750.5 of the Water Code, unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification, or subcontracts with the appropriately licensed contractor.
rules.notes: Fire protection work is normally C-16.

rules.title: B-2 residential remodeling contractor scope
rules.plain_english: A B-2 contractor improves existing wood-frame homes on jobs that use at least three unrelated trades in one contract, such as drywall, flooring, painting, tile, siding, roof repair, or replacing electrical, plumbing and mechanical fixtures. The B-2 may do the work itself or subcontract any trade to licensed subs.

example_trades: installing/repairing/replacing electrical fixtures (dimmers, fans, lights, outlets, switches)
installing/repairing/replacing plumbing fixtures (faucets, sinks, toilets, tubs)
installing/repairing/replacing mechanical fixtures (air filters, air delivery and return grills, preassembled exhaust fans)

rules.applies_to: B-2 license holders and applicants; homeowners hiring remodelers
rules.verbatim_quote: A residential remodeling contractor is a contractor whose principal contracting business is in connection with any project to make improvements to, on, or in an existing residential wood frame structure, and the project requires the use of at least three unrelated building trades or crafts for a single contract.
rules.notes: New construction and non-wood-frame structures are outside B-2 scope. The trade list is non-exhaustive ('may include, but is not limited to').

rules.title: B-2 contract must include three or more unrelated trades
rules.plain_english: A B-2 contractor may not take a contract unless it includes at least three unrelated trades.
rules.verbatim_quote: A residential remodeling contractor shall not take a contract unless the contract includes three or more unrelated trades or crafts.
rules.notes: Check per contract, not per project.

verification.note: 'three or more unrelated trades or crafts' per contract matches; added SB 1189 effective 1/1/2021.

rules.title: B-2 may not contract C-16, C-22 or C-57 work without license or licensed sub
rules.plain_english: A B-2 contractor cannot contract for a job that includes fire protection (C-16), asbestos abatement (C-22) or well drilling (C-57) unless it holds that license or subcontracts that work to a contractor who does.
rules.verbatim_quote: A residential remodeling contractor shall not contract for a project that includes the following trades or crafts unless the contractor holds the appropriate license classification or subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor: (A) C-16 Fire Protection. (B) C-22 Asbestos Abatement. (C) C-57 Well Drilling.

rules.title: B-2 may not contract structural changes to load-bearing elements
rules.plain_english: A B-2 contractor cannot contract to make structural changes to load-bearing parts of an existing building, such as footings, foundations, bearing walls, partitions or roof structures. Unlike the other B-2 limits, there is no subcontracting exception.
rules.verbatim_quote: A residential remodeling contractor shall not contract to make structural changes to load bearing portions of an existing structure, including, but not limited to, footings, foundations, load bearing walls, partitions, and roof structures.
rules.notes: A job that needs load-bearing structural work requires a B (or other suitable) license, not a B-2.

rules.title: B-2 limits on electrical, mechanical and plumbing systems
rules.plain_english: A B-2 contractor cannot contract to install, replace, substantially alter or extend electrical, mechanical or plumbing systems unless it holds the license or subcontracts to a licensed contractor. It may make minor alterations to existing systems to install, repair or replace fixtures, as long as the contract uses at least three unrelated trades.

parameters.restricted_work: install, replace, substantially alter, or extend electrical, mechanical, or plumbing systems or their component parts

minor_alteration_exception.purpose: installing, repairing, or replacing electrical, mechanical and plumbing fixtures

rules.verbatim_quote: The residential remodeling contractor shall not contract to install, replace, substantially alter, or extend electrical, mechanical, or plumbing systems or their component parts, or the mechanisms or devices that are part of those systems, unless the residential remodeling contractor holds the appropriate license classification or subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor.
rules.notes: CSLB may further define 'minor alterations' by regulation (7057.5(c)(3)(C)); check current 16 CCR for the definition.

rules.title: Specialty contractor (C) definition
rules.plain_english: A specialty contractor does construction work in a specialized trade. Specialty work includes servicing or testing fire extinguishing systems, laying carpet and resilient flooring, and setting up or removing roadway work zones, lane closures, flagging and traffic diversions.

included_operations: servicing or testing fire extinguishing systems
installation and laying of carpets, linoleum, and resilient floor covering
preparing or removing roadway construction zones, lane closures, flagging, or traffic diversions on roadways, including public streets, highways, or any public conveyance

rules.verbatim_quote: A specialty contractor is a contractor whose operations involve the performance of construction work requiring special skill and whose principal contracting business involves the use of specialized building trades or crafts.
rules.notes: Traffic control and flagging companies need a contractor license under 7058(d).

rules.title: Asbestos work of 100 sq ft or more needs C-22 or asbestos certification
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not do asbestos-related work involving 100 square feet or more of asbestos-containing material unless it holds the C-22 Asbestos Abatement license or its qualifier has passed the asbestos certification exam. Installing, maintaining or repairing asbestos cement pipe or sheets, vinyl asbestos flooring, or asbestos bituminous or resinous materials does not require the certification exam.

parameters.measure: surface area of asbestos containing materials

rules.verbatim_quote: A contractor shall not engage in asbestos-related work, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, that involves 100 square feet or more of surface area of asbestos containing materials, unless the contractor holds a C-22 Asbestos Abatement classification or the qualifier for the license passes an asbestos certification examination.
rules.notes: CSLB may require updated asbestos certification exams based on new health and safety information. DOSH registration is also required (see asbestos-cert-dosh-registration-90-days).

verification.note: 100 sq ft or more, C-22 or qualifier certification, and the three exam-exempt material types match. The printed section has no '(a)' label before the first paragraph; '(b)' follows.

rules.title: All initial license applicants must complete the asbestos open-book exam
rules.plain_english: Every applicant for an initial contractor license must complete CSLB's open-book asbestos exam and submit it before the license is issued.

parameters.who: all applicants for an initial contractor license
parameters.due: prior to issuance of the license

rules.verbatim_quote: All applicants for an initial contractor license shall complete the open book examination and, prior to the issuance of a contractor’s license, submit it to the board electronically or by mail if the applicant elects to use the hard-copy format.
rules.notes: This is separate from the asbestos certification exam for 100+ sq ft work.

rules.title: Register with Cal/OSHA (DOSH) within 90 days of passing asbestos certification
rules.plain_english: After passing the asbestos certification exam, the contractor must register with the Division of Occupational Safety and Health within 90 days of being notified. If it misses the deadline, CSLB may require it to retake the exam and pay the test fees again.

parameters.trigger: date contractor is notified of passing the asbestos certification exam
parameters.agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Labor Code 6501.5)
parameters.consequence_if_missed: board may require reexamination; test fees apply
parameters.exception: certification may issue without DOSH registration if contractor states in writing it does not perform asbestos-related work

rules.verbatim_quote: The contractor shall register with the division within 90 days from the date the contractor is notified of the passage of the certification examination. The board may require a reexamination if the contractor fails to register within 90 days following issuance of the notification.

verification.note: 90 days from notice of passing; reexamination and test fees on failure; written no-asbestos-work statement exception all match.

rules.title: Show current DOSH asbestos registration at license renewal
rules.plain_english: A contractor certified for asbestos work that actually does asbestos-related work must show proof of current DOSH registration when it renews its contractor license.

parameters.document: proof of current DOSH asbestos registration (Labor Code 6501.5)
parameters.condition: contractor is asbestos-certified and engages in asbestos-related work

rules.verbatim_quote: Any contractor who is certified to engage in asbestos-related work shall present proof of current registration with the division pursuant to Section 6501.5 of the Labor Code upon application for renewal of the contractor’s license, if the contractor engages in asbestos-related work, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code.

rules.title: Non-certified contractor may bid asbestos projects if a qualified contractor does the asbestos work
rules.plain_english: A contractor without asbestos certification can still bid on and contract for a project that includes asbestos work, as long as the asbestos work itself is done by a C-22 contractor or a contractor that is certified and registered with DOSH.

parameters.condition: asbestos-related work performed by a C-22 holder or a certified and DOSH-registered contractor

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors on projects with asbestos-related work
rules.verbatim_quote: A contractor who is not certified pursuant to this section may bid on and contract to perform a project involving asbestos-related work as long as the asbestos-related work is performed by a contractor who holds the C-22 Asbestos Abatement classification or is certified and registered pursuant to this section and Section 6501.5 of the Labor Code.
rules.notes: The book also cross-references H&S Code 25914-25914.3 (separate asbestos/hazardous removal contracts), which are in the Appendix and not covered here.

rules.title: Hazardous substance removal or remedial action needs HAZ certification
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not do a hazardous substance removal or remedial action unless its qualifier has passed the hazardous substance certification exam. The rule covers digging into the earth and removing the dug material at a listed state (DTSC) or federal Superfund (NPL) site, but not asbestos work or highway spill cleanup.

parameters.required: qualifier passed approved hazardous substance certification examination
parameters.covered_activity: removal or remedial action (H&S Code 78000 et seq.) requiring digging into the surface of the earth and removing dug material
covered_sites: site listed under H&S Code 78760 et seq.
excluded: hazardous substance spill on a highway

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing excavation and removal at listed hazardous substance sites
rules.verbatim_quote: No contractor may engage in a removal or remedial action, as defined in subdivision (d), unless the qualifier for the license has passed an approved hazardous substance certification examination.
rules.notes: CSLB may require updated certification exams of current certificate holders.

rules.title: Installing or removing underground storage tanks needs HAZ certification
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not install or remove an underground storage tank unless it has passed the hazardous substance certification exam. A non-certified contractor may bid on or contract for the tank work if a certified contractor does it.

parameters.covered_activity: installation or removal of an underground storage tank (H&S Code 25281(y))
parameters.condition_for_noncertified: work performed by a certified contractor

rules.applies_to: Contractors installing or removing underground storage tanks
rules.verbatim_quote: A contractor may not install or remove an underground storage tank, unless the contractor has passed the hazardous substance certification examination developed pursuant to this section. (2) A contractor who is not certified may bid on or contract for the installation or removal of an underground tank, if the work is performed by a contractor who is certified pursuant to this section.
rules.effective: Amended by Stats 2022 ch 258 (AB 2327), effective January 1, 2023; book history line reads 'operative effective 1/1/2024'

rules.title: Specialty contractors may do other trades only if incidental and supplemental
rules.plain_english: A specialty contractor may take a contract involving several trades, but work outside its own classification must be incidental and supplemental to the work in the trade it is licensed for.

parameters.out_of_class_work_allowed_if: incidental and supplemental to the licensed craft

rules.verbatim_quote: Nothing contained in this section shall prohibit a specialty contractor from taking and executing a contract involving the use of two or more crafts or trades, if the performance of the work in the crafts or trades, other than in which they are licensed, is incidental and supplemental to the performance of the work in the craft for which the specialty contractor is licensed.
rules.notes: 'Incidental and supplemental' is defined further in CSLB regulations (16 CCR 831), not in this text. CSLB may limit a licensee's field and scope to its classifications.

rules.title: Additional classifications: application fee only, no extra license fee
rules.plain_english: A licensee may hold more than one classification if it qualifies for each. Adding a classification requires an application and the application fee, but there is no extra license fee for it.
rules.verbatim_quote: The application shall be in a form as prescribed by the registrar and shall be accompanied by the application fee fixed by this chapter. No license fee shall be charged for an additional classification or classifications.
rules.notes: The fee amount is set in the fee article (B&P 7137), outside this chunk.

verification.note: Application fee required, no license fee for additional classifications. SB 1455 effective 1/1/2025 confirmed in history note.

rules.title: Public works: specialty prime only if its class is a majority of the project
rules.plain_english: On public works, the awarding agency decides which license class is needed to bid and perform. It may never award a prime contract to a specialty contractor whose classification covers less than a majority of the project, and a specialty prime's work outside its class must go to licensed subcontractors under the Subletting and Subcontracting Fair Practices Act.

parameters.out_of_specialty_work: performed by licensed subcontractor per Public Contract Code 4100 et seq., except incidental and supplemental work under 7059(a)

rules.applies_to: Public agencies awarding contracts; specialty contractors bidding public works
rules.verbatim_quote: In no case shall the awarding authority award a prime contract to a specialty contractor whose classification constitutes less than a majority of the project. When a specialty contractor is authorized to bid a project, all work to be performed outside of their license specialty, except work authorized by subdivision (a), shall be performed by a licensed subcontractor
rules.notes: The text does not say how to measure 'majority' (likely by contract value; not stated). Awarding authorities may not set their own contractor qualification regulations (7059(b)(2)).

verification.note: 'less than a majority of the project' bar and Subletting and Subcontracting Fair Practices Act cross-reference match. The text does not define how majority is measured, as the note says.

rules.title: Business name must match classifications and entity type; one name per license
rules.plain_english: A licensee may not use a business name that implies classifications it does not hold or that does not fit its entity type (for example 'Inc.' on a sole owner license). It also may not do business under more than one name per license.
rules.verbatim_quote: A licensee shall not use any business name that indicates the licensee is qualified to perform work in classifications other than those issued for that license, or any business name that is incompatible with the type of business entity licensed. (b) A licensee shall not conduct business under more than one name for each license.
rules.notes: Name changes go through the CSLB change process (see notify-changes-90-days).

rules.title: Who can be licensed; officers and members must be listed as personnel of record
rules.plain_english: Licenses are issued to sole owners, partnerships, corporations, LLCs and participating tribes. Every officer, member, responsible manager or director of a corporation or LLC, and every partner of a partnership, must be listed on the application as personnel of record.
rules.verbatim_quote: Contractors’ licenses are to be issued to individual owners, partnerships, corporations, limited liability companies, and participating tribes, in accordance with this chapter. (A) Every person who is an officer, member, responsible manager, or director of a corporation or limited liability company seeking licensure under this chapter shall be listed on the application

rules.title: Corporations and LLCs must give their Secretary of State ID; tribal businesses must verify status
rules.plain_english: A corporation or LLC (domestic or foreign) applying for a license must give its California Secretary of State identification number. A tribal business must provide proof of its tribal status, such as a charter resolution, articles or bylaws, or a federal tribe listing.

tribal_verification_examples: enacted resolution ratifying charter under Section 17 of the Indian Reorganization Act
enacted resolution authorizing the tribally chartered corporation under tribal law
current federal list of recognized tribes or tribal leadership directory (25 U.S.C. 5131) or BIA website

rules.applies_to: Corporation, LLC and tribal business applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: A corporation or limited liability company, whether foreign or domestic, seeking licensure under this chapter shall provide its identification number issued by the Secretary of State.

rules.title: Who may serve as qualifying individual for each entity type
rules.plain_english: Each license is qualified by a person who has the knowledge and experience. A sole owner qualifies personally or through an RME. A partnership uses a general partner or RME. A corporation or tribe uses an RMO or RME. An LLC uses an RMO, responsible managing manager, responsible managing member or RME.
rules.verbatim_quote: If a corporation, or any other combination or organization, it shall qualify by the appearance of a responsible managing officer or responsible managing employee who is qualified for the same license classification as the classification being applied for.
rules.effective: Amended effective September 28, 2021 (AB 830); 7065 amended effective January 1, 2025

rules.title: No exam if qualifier passed or qualified in same class within prior 5 years
rules.plain_english: A qualifying individual does not have to retake the exam if, within the 5 years before applying, they passed the exam for the same classification or served as qualifier for a license in good standing in that classification.

exempt_if_any: qualifier personally passed written exam for same classification
qualifier served as qualifying individual for a licensee in good standing in same classification at any time in the period

rules.verbatim_quote: No examination shall be required of a qualifying individual if, within the five-year period immediately preceding the application for licensure, the qualifying individual has either personally passed the written examination for the same classification being applied for, or has served as the qualifying individual for a licensee whose license was in good standing
rules.notes: Mandatory ('shall'), unlike the discretionary waivers in 7065.1.

verification.note: Five-year window and both alternatives match. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note (SB 1455, effective 1/1/2025).

rules.title: Limited specialty classification: no trade exam
rules.plain_english: Applicants for the limited specialty classification do not take a trade exam.
rules.verbatim_quote: Notwithstanding Section 7065, no trade examination shall be required of an applicant for the limited specialty license classification.
rules.notes: Only the trade exam is waived; the text does not waive the law and business exam. The limited specialty is the C-61 class under CSLB regulations (not stated here).

rules.title: Exam waiver: listed personnel of a licensee for 5 of the past 7 years
rules.plain_english: CSLB may waive the exam if the qualifier was listed as personnel of record of an active licensee in good standing in the same classification for 5 of the 7 years before applying, and the licensee was actively doing construction in that classification.

conditions: listed on CSLB records as personnel of a licensee
license active and in good standing
licensee actively engaged in construction in that classification during the period

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals seeking an exam waiver
rules.verbatim_quote: The qualifying individual has, for five of the seven years immediately preceding the application for licensure, been listed on the official records of the board as a member of the personnel of any licensee who held a license, which was active and in good standing, in the same classification being applied for,
rules.notes: Waiver is discretionary ('may waive').

verification.note: 5 of 7 years, active and in good standing, same classification, actively engaged; 'may waive' is discretionary.

rules.title: Exam waiver: family member continuing a family business
rules.plain_english: CSLB may waive the exam for an immediate family member of a licensee whose individual license was active and in good standing for 5 of the last 7 years, if the family member worked in the business for 5 of those 7 years, the license is needed to keep the family business going after the licensee's absence or death, and they apply in the same classifications.

conditions: immediate family member of an individual licensee
license needed to continue family business on absence or death of licensee

rules.verbatim_quote: The qualifying individual has been actively engaged in the licensee’s business for five of the seven years immediately preceding the application for licensure. (2) The license is required to continue the existing family business in the event of the absence or death of the licensee.
rules.notes: 'Immediate family member' is defined for license-number reissuance in 7075.1(d); 7065.1 does not define it.

verification.note: Licensee's individual license 5 of 7 years, family member engaged 5 of 7 years, continuation need, same classifications all match.

rules.title: Exam waiver: corporation/LLC employee replacing its qualifier
rules.plain_english: CSLB may waive the exam for a corporation or LLC employee (including officers and managers) who is replacing the company's qualifier, if the employee worked there in a supervisory role in the same classifications for 5 of the last 7 years, the company held an active license in good standing in those classifications for 5 of the last 7 years, and the company has not used this waiver in the past 5 years.
rules.applies_to: Corporations and LLCs replacing a qualifier
rules.verbatim_quote: For five of the seven years immediately preceding the application for licensure, the qualifying individual has been continually employed by the corporation or limited liability company in a supervisory capacity in the same classifications being applied for.

verification.note: 5 of 7 years supervisory employment, 5 of 7 years entity license, no waiver within past five years, officers/managers count as employees.

rules.title: Exam waiver: former California licensee who contracted for the U.S. government
rules.plain_english: CSLB may waive the exam for an applicant who previously held a valid California contractor license and has been working as a contractor for the U.S. government in a license-exempt position.

conditions: previously held a valid California contractor license
acting as a contractor for the United States government in a license-exempt position

rules.applies_to: Former California licensees doing federal work
rules.verbatim_quote: the registrar may waive the examination for a contractor’s license if the applicant has previously held a valid contractor’s license in this state and has been acting in the capacity of a contractor for the United States government in a position exempt from licensure under this chapter.

rules.title: Adding a classification without exam: 5 of 7 years plus 4 years of experience in last 10
rules.plain_english: A licensee can add a classification without an exam if its qualifier was listed as personnel of an active licensee in good standing for 5 of the last 7 years, and has at least 4 years of journeyman, foreman, supervisor or contractor experience in the new classification within the last 10 years. The new class must be closely related to existing classes, or the qualifier must be with an A or B contractor for whom the class is a significant part of the business.

relatedness_test: qualifier associated with licensed A or B contractor and class is a significant component of its business

rules.verbatim_quote: The qualifying individual for the applicant has had within the last 10 years immediately preceding the filing of the application, not less than four years experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee, or contractor in the classification within which the licensee intends to engage in the additional classification as a contractor.
rules.notes: Requires a 'conclusive showing' of experience satisfactory to the registrar. At least 3% of these applications get a full investigation.

verification.note: 5 of 7 years personnel listing, not less than 4 years experience within last 10 years, relatedness test, limited-specialty exclusion and 'no less than 3 percent' audit all match. SB 822 effective 1/1/2014 confirmed.

rules.title: Reciprocity: trade exam waivable with 5 years good standing in a reciprocal state
rules.plain_english: CSLB may accept an out-of-state contractor's qualifications in a similar classification if that state gives California licensees the same treatment and has equal or stricter standards. The trade exam may be waived if the other state certifies in writing that the license has been in good standing for the previous 5 years.

parameters.document: written certification from the other state
conditions: licensed in similar classification in other state
other state reciprocates for California licensees
other state's standards at least equal (case-by-case)

rules.applies_to: Out-of-state licensed contractors applying in California
rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar may waive the trade examination for that applicant if the applicant provides written certification from that other state in which he or she is licensed, that the applicant’s license has been in good standing for the previous five years.
rules.notes: Only the trade exam is mentioned; the law and business exam is not waived by this section.

verification.note: Written certification of good standing for previous five years; only the trade examination is named. Effective 9/25/1990 confirmed.

rules.title: No license to or through a minor without a court-appointed guardian
rules.plain_english: A minor cannot be licensed, and no partnership, corporation, LLC or other business with a minor as a partner, officer, director, manager or RME can be licensed, unless a court has appointed a guardian for the minor.

applies_if_minor_is: holder of any responsible official position
parameters.exception: guardian appointed by court of competent jurisdiction

rules.verbatim_quote: No license shall be issued to a minor, nor to any partnership a partner of which is a minor, nor to any corporation any officer, director or responsible managing employee of which is a minor, nor to any limited liability company any officer, manager, or responsible managing employee of which is a minor

rules.title: Applications must be signed by applicant and qualifier; e-signatures allowed
rules.plain_english: Every original, renewal, reinstatement or reissuance application, active or inactive, must be on the CSLB form with the fee, and must be signed by both the applicant and the qualifying individual. CSLB may accept electronic filing and digital signatures.
rules.verbatim_quote: Every application form for an original license, for renewal thereof, for reinstatement or for reissuance, including both active and inactive licenses, shall be signed by both the applicant and by the person qualifying on behalf of an individual or firm as referred to in Section 7068.1.

rules.title: Applicants must show trade experience and knowledge of building, safety, health and lien laws
rules.plain_english: Applicants must show knowledge and experience in the classification and general knowledge of California building, safety, health and lien laws and contracting business principles. The written exam includes questions on state law and the contracting business, and an applicant qualifying through an RME must also show this law and business knowledge.

required_knowledge: trade knowledge and experience in classification

rules.verbatim_quote: The board shall require an applicant to show the degree of knowledge and experience in the classification applied for, and the general knowledge of the building, safety, health, and lien laws of the state and of the administrative principles of the contracting business that the board deems necessary for the safety and protection of the public.
rules.notes: The years of experience needed are set by CSLB regulation (16 CCR 825), not in this text.

rules.title: RME must be a permanent employee working 32 hrs/week or 80% of business hours
rules.plain_english: A responsible managing employee must be a permanent, bona fide employee who is actively engaged in the work they qualify for. Actively engaged means working 32 hours a week, or 80% of the hours the business is open each week, whichever is less.

parameters.employment_type: permanently employed by the applicant (bona fide employee)

rules.applies_to: Licensees qualified by a responsible managing employee (RME)
rules.verbatim_quote: “Bona fide employee of the applicant” means an employee who is permanently employed by the applicant. (B) “Actively engaged” means working 32 hours per week, or 80 percent of the total hours per week that the applicant’s business is in operation, whichever is less.
rules.notes: Useful check for HR/payroll: RME timesheets should meet the computed minimum.

verification.note: 32 hours/week or 80% of business hours, whichever is less; 'permanently employed' definition matches. AB 830 effective 9/28/2021 confirmed.

rules.title: Qualifier may not hold another active license (except under 7068.1)
rules.plain_english: A person serving as qualifier for a licensee may not hold any other active contractor license at the same time, except as allowed by the multiple-license rules in 7068.1.

parameters.exception: B&P 7068.1 (20% common ownership, subsidiary/joint venture, or same majority officers; max 3 firms per year)

rules.verbatim_quote: Except in accordance with Section 7068.1, no person qualifying on behalf of an individual or firm under paragraph (1), (2), (3), or (4) of subdivision (b) shall hold any other active contractor’s license while acting in the capacity of a qualifying individual pursuant to this section.

verification.note: Extra check (numeric prohibition): no other active license except under 7068.1.

rules.title: Qualifier must file a statement verifying their role at each renewal
rules.plain_english: At every renewal, the current qualifying individual must file a CSLB form confirming they still serve as the licensee's qualifier.

parameters.document: statement on registrar form verifying capacity as qualifying individual

rules.verbatim_quote: At the time of application for renewal of a license, the current qualifying individual shall file a statement with the registrar, on a form prescribed by the registrar, verifying their capacity as a qualifying individual to the licensee.

rules.title: Experience claims must be verified by a qualified, responsible person
rules.plain_english: An applicant's claimed experience must be certified by a qualified and responsible person, and CSLB randomly audits a share of these statements. Experience gained in other states counts only if it was gained lawfully in that state.
rules.verbatim_quote: Statements made by or on behalf of an applicant as to the applicant’s experience in the classification applied for shall be verified by a qualified and responsible person.
rules.notes: The audit percentage is set by regulation, not stated here. Unlicensed out-of-state work where a license was required may not count.

rules.title: Qualifier must exercise supervision and control of construction operations
rules.plain_english: The qualifying individual is responsible for supervising and controlling the company's construction work so it complies with the license law. That means supervising operations, making technical and administrative decisions, checking jobs for workmanship, or supervising job sites, or monitoring and being available to people they delegate to. Applicants must describe the qualifier's duties in detail.

parameters.supervision_and_control: direct supervision or control, or monitoring and being available to assist others to whom direct supervision and control has been delegated
direct_supervision_or_control_any_of: managing construction activities by making technical and administrative decisions
parameters.required_document: detailed information on qualifier duties and responsibilities (7068.1(d))

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals and the licensees they qualify
rules.verbatim_quote: The person qualifying on behalf of an individual or firm under paragraph (1), (2), (3), or (4) of subdivision (b) of Section 7068 shall be responsible for exercising supervision and control of their employer’s or principal’s construction operations to secure compliance with this chapter and the rules and regulations of the board.
rules.notes: 'Firm' covers partnerships, limited partnerships, corporations, LLCs and other organizations.

rules.title: Qualifying more than one firm needs 20% common ownership, subsidiary/JV, or same majority officers
rules.plain_english: A qualifier may qualify an additional firm only if at least 20% of the equity of each firm is under common ownership, the additional firm is a subsidiary (at least 20% owned) or joint venture of the first, or a majority of the partners, officers or managers are the same.

allowed_if_any: at least 20% common ownership of equity of each firm
additional firm is a subsidiary (>=20% equity owned) or joint venture of the first
majority of partners, officers, or managers are the same

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals serving more than one licensee
rules.verbatim_quote: There is a common ownership of at least 20 percent of the equity of each individual or firm for which the person acts in a qualifying capacity. (2) The additional firm is a subsidiary of or a joint venture with the first. “Subsidiary,” as used in this subdivision, means any firm at least 20 percent of the equity of which is owned by the other firm.
rules.notes: Changes to this multiple-license exemption must be reported to CSLB within 90 days (7083).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 287 (B&P 7068.1(a)(1)-(3)); PDF page 323 (B&P 7083(a))
verification.note: 20% common equity, subsidiary at least 20% owned or JV, same majority of partners/officers/managers match. The 90-day change report in the note is confirmed by 7083(a).

rules.title: A qualifier may qualify no more than three firms in any one-year period
rules.plain_english: Even when the ownership tests are met, one person can serve as qualifier for no more than three firms in any one-year period.
rules.verbatim_quote: Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) to (3), inclusive, of subdivision (a), a qualifying individual may act as the qualifier for no more than three firms in any one-year period.
rules.notes: Count all firms qualified during any rolling 12-month window.

verification.note: 'no more than three firms in any one-year period' matches. The rolling-window reading in the note is an interpretation; the text says only 'any one-year period'.

rules.title: Qualifier rule violations: misdemeanor, up to 6 months jail and $3,000-$5,000 fine
rules.plain_english: Breaking the qualifier rules (for example, being an absentee qualifier or qualifying too many firms) is cause for discipline and a misdemeanor punishable by up to 6 months in county jail, a fine of $3,000 to $5,000, or both.
rules.verbatim_quote: Violation of this section shall constitute a cause for disciplinary action and shall be punishable as a misdemeanor by imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed six months, by a fine of not less than three thousand dollars ($3,000), but not to exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000), or by both the fine and imprisonment.

verification.note: Up to six months county jail, fine $3,000-$5,000, or both; also cause for discipline. SB 1455 effective 1/1/2025 confirmed.

rules.title: Report qualifier departure to CSLB in writing within 90 days
rules.plain_english: When the RMO, RME, responsible managing member or manager leaves, the licensee or the qualifier must notify CSLB in writing within 90 days. If no one notifies CSLB in time, the license is suspended (or the classification removed) and the qualifier removed as of the date CSLB receives the notice, and the late notice is grounds for discipline.

parameters.trigger: date of qualifier disassociation
parameters.consequence_if_late: automatic suspension or classification removal, effective date written notice received at CSLB headquarters; grounds for discipline

rules.applies_to: All licensees with an RMO, RME, responsible managing member or responsible managing manager
rules.verbatim_quote: If the responsible managing officer, responsible managing employee, responsible managing member, or responsible managing manager disassociates from the licensed entity, the licensee or the qualifier shall notify the registrar in writing within 90 days after the date of disassociation.

verification.note: 90-day written notice by licensee or qualifier; suspension/classification removal effective on HQ receipt; grounds for discipline. SB 1171 effective 1/1/2013 confirmed.

rules.title: Replace a departed qualifier within 90 days or the license is suspended
rules.plain_english: The licensee has 90 days from the qualifier's departure to replace them by filing an application and fee naming a new qualifier. If not replaced in time, the license is automatically suspended (or the classification removed) at the end of the 90 days.

parameters.trigger: date of qualifier disassociation
parameters.required_filing: application to replace qualifier plus fee
parameters.consequence_if_missed: automatic suspension of license or removal of classification at day 90

rules.verbatim_quote: The licensee shall have 90 days after the date of disassociation in which to replace the qualifier. Upon failure to replace the qualifier within 90 days after the date of disassociation, the license shall be automatically suspended or the classification removed at the end of the 90 days.
rules.notes: If the departed person qualified only one of several classifications, that classification is removed instead of the whole license being suspended.

verification.note: 90 days to replace; automatic suspension or classification removal at day 90; application plus fee. The note's single-classification reading is an interpretation of 'or the classification removed'; the text does not say when each applies.

rules.title: Departing qualifier stays responsible until the later of departure or CSLB's receipt of notice
rules.plain_english: A qualifier remains responsible for the licensee's construction operations until the later of the date they left or the date CSLB receives written notice. Qualifiers should send their own notice promptly.
rules.verbatim_quote: The person qualifying on behalf of a licensee under Section 7068 shall be responsible for the licensee's construction operations until the date of disassociation or the date the board receives the written notification of disassociation, whichever is later.

verification.note: 'whichever is later' matches. Blank 'effective' filled from the 7068.2 history note (SB 1171, effective 1/1/2013).

rules.title: One 90-day extension to replace a qualifier (180-day cap for date disputes or death)
rules.plain_english: For good cause, CSLB may grant one 90-day extension to replace a qualifier if the licensee disputes the departure date, the qualifier died, or processing was delayed by CSLB or another agency. The petition must arrive within 90 days of the departure, death or delay, and a replacement application must already be on file. For date disputes or death, the total time to replace is capped at 180 days.

parameters.petition_trigger: date of disassociation, death, or delay
grounds: processing delay outside applicant's control caused by CSLB or another state or federal agency
parameters.prerequisite: application to replace qualifier on file

rules.verbatim_quote: The petition shall only be considered if an application to replace the qualifier as prescribed by the registrar is on file with the board. Under the circumstances described in subparagraphs (A) and (B) of paragraph (1), the licensee shall have no more than a total of 180 days after the date of disassociation or death in which to replace the qualifier.
rules.notes: The text sets no 180-day cap for the agency-delay ground.

verification.note: One 90-day extension, three grounds, petition received within 90 days of disassociation/death/delay, replacement application on file, 180-day total cap only for grounds (A) and (B).

rules.title: Taking or obtaining a CSLB exam for someone else is a misdemeanor
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor for anyone other than the named examinee to take the qualifying exam for an applicant, or for anyone without authorization to obtain and give another person the exam or any part of it.

prohibited_acts: taking the qualifying exam on behalf of an applicant
obtaining and providing the exam or any part of it to another without authorization

rules.verbatim_quote: It is a misdemeanor for any person other than the examinee named in the application to take the qualifying examination on behalf of an applicant for a contractor’s license.
rules.notes: No specific fine is stated in these sections.

verification.note: Both misdemeanors match; neither section states a fine. Blank 'effective' filled from the history notes.

rules.title: Applicant and all officers, partners, managers and RMEs must be free of B&P 480 grounds
rules.plain_english: The applicant and each officer, director, partner, manager, associate and RME must not have committed acts or crimes that are grounds for denial under B&P 480. For entity applicants, the license is refused if any officer, director, partner, LLC manager or member fails the non-experience qualifications.

parameters.standard: no acts or crimes that are grounds for denial under B&P 480

rules.applies_to: All applicants and their personnel of record
rules.verbatim_quote: An applicant, and each officer, director, partner, manager, associate, and responsible managing employee thereof, shall not have committed acts or crimes that are grounds for denial of licensure under Section 480.
rules.notes: B&P 480 limits (look-back periods, rehabilitation) appear in an earlier section of the book.

rules.title: Applicants must submit fingerprints for DOJ and FBI background checks
rules.plain_english: Applicants must provide a full set of fingerprints, electronically (Live Scan) if available, for California DOJ and FBI criminal history checks. CSLB may also receive later arrest information.

parameters.format: electronic if readily available; alternatives require registrar approval

rules.verbatim_quote: As part of an application for a contractor’s license, the board shall require an applicant to furnish a full set of fingerprints for purposes of conducting a criminal history record check.
rules.notes: This subdivision says only 'an applicant'. Whether each officer, partner and qualifier must also be fingerprinted is not stated here (7069(a) does screen all of them), so confirm current CSLB practice.

rules.title: Proof of arrest disposition due within 90 days when CSLB asks
rules.plain_english: If CSLB learns a member of a licensee's personnel or a home improvement salesperson was arrested, it may demand proof of how the case ended, such as certified court records. The proof must reach CSLB within 90 days of the disposition or 90 days of CSLB's demand, whichever is later. Failing to comply is cause for discipline.

who: personnel of record of a licensee

rules.applies_to: Licensee personnel and registered home improvement salespersons
rules.verbatim_quote: Any proof required by this section shall be received by the registrar within 90 days of the date of the disposition, or within 90 days of the registrar’s demand for information if that date is later.
rules.notes: The demand is sent by first-class mail to the last official address of record, so keeping the address current matters.

verification.note: 90 days of disposition or of registrar's demand, whichever is later; first-class mail demand; cause for discipline.

rules.title: After a denial, reapply no earlier than one year unless CSLB sets an earlier date
rules.plain_english: An applicant must show it was never denied a license or had one revoked for reasons that bar the new license. When CSLB denies an application, the earliest reapplication date is one year from the decision or notice, unless CSLB sets an earlier date.

parameters.trigger: effective date of denial decision or service of notice under B&P 485(b)

rules.verbatim_quote: inform the applicant of the earliest date that the applicant may reapply for a license, which shall be one year from the effective date of the decision or service of notice under subdivision (b) of Section 485, unless the board prescribes an earlier date.
rules.notes: For crime-related denials, 7073(b) caps the wait at 5 years; see denial-crime-reapply-max-5-years.

verification.note: One year from the decision's effective date or service of 485(b) notice, unless the board sets an earlier date.

rules.title: Licensee entering the military: name a designee within 30 days
rules.plain_english: A licensee entering the U.S. armed forces may name responsible managing person(s) to run the business until one year after discharge. The license stays in force for 30 days after entry, and the designees must be reported to CSLB before those 30 days end. Renewal fees must still be paid.

parameters.designee_report_deadline: before expiration of 30 days after entry into armed forces

rules.verbatim_quote: Any license shall remain in full force and effect for 30 days after the entrance of the licensee into the armed forces, but he shall prior to the expiration of such 30-day period provide the registrar with the name or names of the persons so designated to conduct his business.

verification.note: License in force 30 days after entry; designees named before the 30 days end; authority until one year after discharge; renewal fee payable. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note.

rules.title: License bonds: admitted surety bond or cash/cashier's check deposit only (no CDs)
rules.plain_english: Required license bonds must be either a bond from an admitted surety insurer or a deposit of cash or a cashier's check with CSLB under CCP 995.710(a)(1). Certificates of deposit and other alternatives are not accepted. CSLB stopped accepting other alternatives on January 1, 2019, and existing ones had to be replaced by January 1, 2020.

allowed_forms: bond executed by admitted surety insurer
lawful money or cashier's check deposited with registrar (CCP 995.710(a)(1))

rules.applies_to: All licensees subject to bond requirements
rules.verbatim_quote: Notwithstanding Article 7 (commencing with Section 995.710) of Chapter 2 of Title 14 of Part 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, no other method of deposit, including, but not limited to, a certificate of deposit, shall satisfy a bond requirement under this article.
rules.notes: The 2026 amendment (AB 521) touches this section; the book does not mark which subdivisions changed.

verification.note: Extra check (dates): admitted surety or CCP 995.710(a)(1) deposit only, no CDs; operative 1/1/2019; existing alternatives replaced by 1/1/2020; 7159.5 equivalents excluded.

rules.title: Cash bond deposits are frozen once CSLB is notified of a lawsuit; shared pro rata if short
rules.plain_english: If CSLB gets written notice of a civil action against a cash deposit given in place of a bond, none of it is released except as a court orders. If the deposit cannot pay all adjudicated claims in full, it is split among claimants in proportion to their claims. CSLB charges no legal fees against it.

parameters.freeze_trigger: written notice to CSLB of civil action against the deposit

rules.applies_to: Licensees with cash deposits in lieu of bond; claimants
rules.verbatim_quote: If the board is notified, in writing, of a civil action against the deposit authorized under this section, the deposit or any portion thereof shall not be released for any purpose, except as determined by the court.

rules.title: Non-wage claims against cash deposits: 3-year deadline
rules.plain_english: A non-wage claim against a cash deposit given in place of a contractor's or qualifier's bond must be filed within 3 years after the license period in which the act happened ends, or within 3 years of the license being inactivated, canceled or revoked, whichever comes first. For a deposit in place of a disciplinary bond, a third deadline also applies: 3 years after the last date the deposit was required.

parameters.deadline_rule: earliest of: (expiration of license period in which act occurred + 3 years), (date license inactivated/canceled/revoked + 3 years), and for disciplinary-bond deposits (last date deposit required + 3 years)
applies_to_deposits: in lieu of qualifying individual bond
parameters.covers: alternatives filed before 2019-01-01 and cash/cashier's check deposits after 2019-01-01

rules.applies_to: Claimants against contractor cash deposits; licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: against a deposit given in lieu of a contractor’s bond or bond of a qualifying individual filed by an active licensee shall be brought within three years after the expiration of the license period during which the act or omission occurred, or within three years of the date the license of the active licensee was inactivated, canceled, or revoked by the board, whichever occurs first.
rules.notes: Surety bonds have a 2-year deadline (7071.11(c)); cash deposits have 3 years.

verification.note: Three-year periods, 'whichever occurs first' / 'whichever date is first', wage claims excluded, and the pre-2019 alternatives / post-2019 cash deposits scope all match. AB 521 effective 1/1/2026 confirmed.

rules.title: Wage and fringe benefit claims against bonds or deposits: 6 months from discovery, 2-year outside limit
rules.plain_english: A claim against a contractor bond or cash deposit for unpaid wages or fringe benefits must be brought within 6 months after the delinquency is discovered. A civil action may never be filed more than 2 years after the wages or contributions were due.
rules.applies_to: Employees, union trust funds and licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: A claim to recover wages or fringe benefits shall be brought within six months from the date that the wage or fringe benefit delinquencies were discovered, but in no event shall a civil action thereon be brought later than two years from the date the wage or fringe benefit contributions were due.
rules.notes: Identical wording appears in both sections, one for cash deposits and one for surety bonds.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 293 (B&P 7071.4(f)(3)); PDF page 301 (B&P 7071.11(d))
verification.note: Six months from discovery, civil action no later than two years from due date; identical wording in both sections.

rules.title: Wage claims against cash deposits go to the Labor Commissioner; 10-day and 60-day payment windows
rules.plain_english: Employee wage and fringe claims against a cash deposit are filed with the Labor Commissioner, who holds a hearing. CSLB waits 10 days after the findings before paying. If a party gives notice that it will seek judicial review and files suit, payment waits for the court. If no action is filed within 60 days of the findings, CSLB pays the claimant.

parameters.judicial_review_notice: written notice of intent to seek review under Gov Code 11523, filed with registrar and commissioner within the 10 days

rules.applies_to: Licensees with cash deposits; employees and employee organizations
rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar shall not make payment from the deposit on the basis of findings by the commissioner for a period of 10 days following determination of the findings.

verification.note: Extra check (numeric process step): 10-day payment hold after findings; written intent to seek review within that period; payment if no action filed within 60 days.

rules.title: Who the contractor's bond protects
rules.plain_english: The contractor's bond protects: homeowners hurt by license-law violations on home improvement to their own home; owners building a single-family home not meant for sale; anyone hurt by willful and deliberate violations or fraud; employees owed wages; and trust funds or others owed fringe benefits.

beneficiaries: homeowner contracting for home improvement on personal family residence
property owner contracting for construction of single-family dwelling not intended or offered for sale when damages incurred
person damaged by willful and deliberate violation or by fraud in execution or performance of a construction contract
employee damaged by failure to pay wages
person or entity (including Civil Code 8024(b) laborer) damaged by failure to pay fringe benefits, public or private work

rules.applies_to: Licensees, homeowners, owners, employees, trust funds
rules.verbatim_quote: The contractor’s bond shall be for the benefit of the following: (a) A homeowner contracting for home improvement upon the homeowner’s personal family residence damaged as a result of a violation of this chapter by the licensee. (b) A property owner contracting for the construction of a single-family dwelling who is damaged as a result of a violation of this chapter by the licensee.
rules.notes: Fringe benefit damages are limited to actual employer payments owed (e.g., Labor Code 1773.1 payments).

rules.title: Contractor's bond: $25,000
rules.plain_english: To get, reinstate, reactivate, renew or keep a license, every licensee must have a $25,000 contractor's bond on file with CSLB. No bond is needed while the license is inactive.
rules.verbatim_quote: The board shall require as a condition precedent to the issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued maintenance of a license, that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a contractor’s bond in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000).
rules.notes: The earlier version of 7071.6 was repealed January 1, 2023 and replaced by this one; the book does not print the earlier amount.

verification.note: $25,000 for issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal or continued maintenance; not required while inactive; current version operative 1/1/2023.

rules.title: Non-homeowner claims against the $25,000 bond capped at $7,500 total
rules.plain_english: Claimants other than homeowners doing home improvement on their own residence can collect no more than $7,500 in total from the contractor's bond (or the qualifier's bond). The rest is reserved for those homeowners, who can recover up to the full bond.

parameters.homeowner_beneficiary: 7071.5(a) homeowner, home improvement on personal family residence

rules.verbatim_quote: Excluding the claims brought by the beneficiaries specified in subdivision (a) of Section 7071.5, the aggregate liability of a surety on claims brought against a bond required by this section shall not exceed the sum of seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500).
rules.notes: reserved_for_homeowners_usd is computed (25,000 - 7,500). Wage and fringe claims have a separate $4,000 aggregate cap (7071.11(a)).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 295 (B&P 7071.6(b)); PDF page 299 (B&P 7071.9(b)); PDF page 294 (B&P 7071.5(a))
verification.note: $7,500 aggregate cap excludes 7071.5(a) homeowner claims; excess reserved for them; they may recover the full bond. Same structure in 7071.9(b) for the qualifier bond.

rules.title: Applicants with past unlicensed-contracting violations may need a $50,000 bond
rules.plain_english: CSLB may require an applicant to post twice the normal contractor's bond, until first renewal, if the applicant was convicted of unlicensed contracting (7028) or got a final citation for it (7028.7), and the violation caused substantial injury to the public.

conditions_all: convicted under B&P 7028 or cited under B&P 7028.7
citation (if any) is a final order of the registrar
violation caused substantial injury to the public

rules.applies_to: Applicants with prior unlicensed contracting violations
rules.verbatim_quote: the board may require an applicant to post a contractor’s bond in twice the amount required pursuant to subdivision (a) until the time that the license is renewed, under the following conditions: (1) The applicant has either been convicted of a violation of Section 7028 or has been cited pursuant to Section 7028.7.
rules.notes: amount_usd is computed as 2 x $25,000.

verification.note: Twice the 7071.6(a) amount until renewal; all three conditions match; 'may require' is discretionary.

rules.title: LLC licensees: extra $100,000 worker protection bond
rules.plain_english: An LLC licensee must also keep a $100,000 surety bond protecting workers owed wages, interest on wages or fringe benefits. If the LLC is party to a collective bargaining agreement, the bond also covers welfare, pension and apprenticeship fund contributions. It is not required while the license is inactive.
rules.verbatim_quote: The board shall require, as a condition precedent to the issuance, reissuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued valid use of a limited liability company license, that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a surety bond in the sum of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000).

verification.note: $100,000; wages, interest on wages, fringe benefits; CBA welfare/pension/apprentice contributions; not required while inactive. SB 392 effective 1/1/2011 confirmed.

rules.title: File a bond within 90 days of its effective date for retroactive reinstatement
rules.plain_english: CSLB accepts a contractor's, LLC, disciplinary or qualifier bond as of the effective date on the bond if it receives the bond within 90 days of that date, and reinstates the license back to that date. A bond received later is still accepted as of its effective date only if the licensee shows the gap was beyond its control.

parameters.trigger: effective date shown on bond
parameters.result_if_timely: accepted as of bond effective date; license reinstated retroactively if otherwise eligible
parameters.late_exception: showing on registrar form that lapse was due to circumstances beyond licensee's control

rules.verbatim_quote: the registrar shall accept a bond required by Section 7071.6, 7071.6.5, 7071.8, or 7071.9 as of the effective date shown on the bond, if the bond is received by the registrar within 90 days after that date, and shall reinstate the license to which the bond pertains, if otherwise eligible, retroactive to the effective date of the bond.
rules.notes: Tool idea: alert when a replacement bond has not been filed within 90 days of its effective date.

verification.note: Four bond sections listed, 90 days after effective date, retroactive reinstatement, beyond-control exception all match.

rules.title: Disciplinary bond: $25,000 to $250,000 after suspension or revocation
rules.plain_english: A person or firm tied to a suspended or revoked license (including the qualifier at the time, and officers who knew or took part) must post a disciplinary bond to get, renew or restore a license, change officers, lift a suspension, or keep using a license under stayed discipline. CSLB sets the amount by how serious the violation was, from $25,000 up to 10 times the contractor's bond.

subject_persons: person whose license was suspended or revoked
qualifier at any time cause for discipline occurred (knowledge not required)
officer, director, manager, partner or personnel of record who knew of or participated in the act
firm whose existing or new personnel had a license suspended or revoked
firm whose personnel held such a role at a disciplined licensee and knew of or participated in the act
triggers: change of officers or members of corporation or LLC
continued valid use of license under stayed discipline

rules.applies_to: Disciplined licensees and their personnel, including new firms they join
rules.verbatim_quote: that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a contractor’s bond in a sum to be fixed by the registrar based upon the seriousness of the violation, but which sum shall not be less than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) nor more than 10 times that amount required by Section 7071.6.
rules.notes: max_usd is computed as 10 x the $25,000 bond in 7071.6. Wage and fringe claims against this bond are not subject to the $4,000 cap in 7071.11(a).

verification.note: Not less than $25,000 nor more than 10 times the 7071.6 amount ($250,000 computed); one disciplinary bond per application or license; subject persons and triggers match.

rules.title: Disciplinary bond stays on file at least 2 years of active, good-standing license time
rules.plain_english: A disciplinary bond must stay on file for at least 2 years, plus any extra time CSLB sets. The clock runs only while the license is current, active and in good standing, so inactive or suspended time does not count.
rules.applies_to: Licensees subject to a disciplinary bond

rules.title: Qualifier's bond: $25,000 when the qualifier is not the owner or a general partner

rules.title: Wage and fringe claims against a license bond capped at $4,000 total

rules.title: No renewal while a judgment or admitted claim above the bond amount is unpaid

rules.title: Non-wage claims against a surety license bond: 2-year deadline

rules.title: Surety must report bond payments to CSLB within 30 days

rules.title: Licensee gets at least 15 days to protest a good-faith bond payment

specific and reasonable basis for opposition

rules.title: No protest: reimburse the surety within 90 days of CSLB notice or license is suspended
rules.plain_english: If the licensee does not protest, it has 90 days from CSLB's notice to prove it repaid the surety, plus any judgment or admitted claim above the bond. Otherwise the license is suspended by law at day 90, and the suspension is shown publicly indefinitely as a failure to settle final liabilities.

proof_required: payment of actual amount owed to surety
payment of any judgment or admitted claim exceeding bond (if applicable)

rules.title: Unreimbursed surety blocks renewal of the license and other licenses with the same personnel

rules.title: Payment plan (accord) with the surety: breaking it means automatic suspension

parameters.consequence_of_breach: automatic suspension by operation of law
parameters.reinstatement_requires: proof of satisfaction of all debts

verification.note: Notarized accord, automatic suspension on breach, reinstatement only on proof all debts satisfied, no board legal fees against the bond. Blank 'effective' filled from the history note.

rules.title: Do not mention the license bond in advertising or solicitations
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not mention any CSLB-required bond in its advertising, sales pitches or other presentations to the public. Doing so is grounds for license suspension.

rules.title: Denying a license bond for race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry or sex: actual damages plus $250

rules.title: Failing to keep a sufficient bond: suspension or revocation

rules.title: Report any unsatisfied final judgment to CSLB within 90 days

rules.title: Report felony or related criminal convictions to CSLB within 90 days

rules.title: LLC licensees: liability insurance of $1M aggregate, more with more than 5 personnel, max $5M

With more than 5, it must add $100,000 per person listed, but never more than $5 million per policy period.
