rules.verbatim_quote: shall be signed by the licensee and shall set forth the license number of the licensee and the facts that constitute the reportable event. If the reportable event involves the action of a court, the report shall also set forth the following: (1) The title of the matter. (2) The court or agency name. (3) The docket number. (4) The claim or file number.
rules.notes: Good candidate for a generated report form.

rules.title: Contractor's CGL, defect or professional liability insurer reports qualifying payments within 30 days
rules.plain_english: An insurer that pays all or part of a judgment, settlement or award meeting the 7071.20 criteria must report it to CSLB within 30 days, with the licensee's name and license number, claim number, total amount, amount the insurer paid, and the payee.

parameters.who: insurer providing commercial general liability, construction defect, or professional liability insurance
parameters.trigger: insurer payment (all or part) of qualifying judgment, settlement, or award

rules.applies_to: Insurers of licensees; licensees (their insurer's report may trigger CSLB review)
rules.verbatim_quote: An insurer providing a licensee commercial general liability insurance, construction defect insurance, or professional liability insurance shall report to the registrar within 30 days of all or a portion of the insurer’s payment of a civil action judgment, settlement payment, or arbitration award, that meets all of the requirements of Section 7071.20,
rules.notes: The licensee's own 90-day duty (7071.20) applies regardless of the insurer report.

verification.note: CGL, construction defect or professional liability insurer; 30 days of payment; five content items match.

rules.title: CSLB notifies within 15 days of approval; license issues when the initial fee is paid
rules.plain_english: Within 15 days after approving an application, CSLB notifies the applicant that the license can be issued once the initial license fee is paid, and issues the license when the fee is paid.

parameters.trigger: approval of application
parameters.next_step: pay initial license fee (Article 8, B&P 7135 et seq.)

rules.verbatim_quote: the registrar, within 15 days after approval of the application, shall notify the applicant that a license may be issued to him on payment of the initial license fee provided in Article 8 (commencing at Section 7135), and, when the initial license fee is paid, shall issue a license to him
rules.notes: Applicant must pay the initial license fee within 90 days of notice or the application is void (7074(a)(2)).

verification.note: Extra check (numeric process step): notice within 15 days after approval; initial fee within 90 days of notice or application void.

rules.title: Return pocket license cards within 5 days of suspension, revocation, denial of renewal or departure
rules.plain_english: All pocket license cards must be returned to CSLB within 5 days of a suspension, revocation or denial of renewal. When a partner, officer or manager leaves a company, they surrender their card to the company, and the company must mail or deliver it to CSLB within 5 days.

triggers: cardholder leaves non-individual licensee (deadline runs after surrender to licensee)

rules.applies_to: Licensees and their partners, officers and managers
rules.verbatim_quote: All cards issued shall be surrendered upon the suspension, revocation, or denial of renewal of the license, and shall be mailed or delivered to the board within five days of the suspension, revocation, or denial.

verification.note: Five days after suspension, revocation or denial of renewal; departing cardholder surrenders to licensee, which mails within five days; card issued at no cost.

rules.title: Crime-based denial: CSLB sets a reapply date no more than 5 years out
rules.plain_english: CSLB may deny an application for failing to follow its rules or on B&P 480 grounds. If the denial is for a crime substantially related to contracting, CSLB must state the earliest date the applicant can reapply, no more than 5 years after the decision, and all evidence of rehabilitation is considered on reapplication.

parameters.trigger: effective date of decision or service of notice under B&P 485(b)
grounds_for_denial: failure to comply with CSLB rule or regulation

rules.verbatim_quote: The date set by the registrar shall not be more than five years from the effective date of the decision or service of notice under subdivision (b) of Section 485.

verification.note: Reapply date not more than five years from decision or 485(b) notice; rehabilitation criteria served. Amended effective 1/1/2006 confirmed.

rules.title: Probationary license instead of denial; 30 days to show cause before revocation
rules.plain_english: Instead of denying an application, CSLB may issue a probationary license with conditions. If problems come up during probation, CSLB notifies the licensee to show cause within 30 days why the license should not be revoked, and the license cannot be renewed while proceedings are pending.

parameters.procedure: Administrative Procedure Act (Gov Code 11500 et seq.)

rules.applies_to: Applicants with criminal or compliance history
rules.verbatim_quote: In lieu of denying licensure as authorized under this section, the registrar may issue an applicant a probationary license with terms and conditions.

verification.note: Show cause within 30 days; APA procedure; no renewal while proceeding pending.

rules.title: Application voids if the exam is not passed within 18 months of acceptance
rules.plain_english: An application for an original license, added classification or new qualifier becomes void if the applicant or examinee does not pass the exam within 18 months after CSLB accepts the application. A new application and fee are then required.

parameters.trigger: date application deemed acceptable by CSLB
parameters.consequence: application void; reapplication fee required; voided application not returned

rules.verbatim_quote: The applicant or the examinee for the applicant has failed to achieve a passing grade in the qualifying examination within 18 months after the application has been deemed acceptable by the board.

verification.note: 18 months after the application is deemed acceptable; original, additional classification or change of qualifier; voided application retained; reapplication fee. Amended effective 1/1/2019 confirmed (history on PDF page 315).

rules.title: Application voids if the fee, bond or documents are not filed within 90 days of notice
rules.plain_english: An application becomes void if, after notice, the applicant does not pay the initial license fee within 90 days, does not file the required bond (or cash deposit) or other documents within 90 days, or does not return a rejected application within 90 days. It is also void if withdrawn or denied after disciplinary proceedings.

triggers.item: file bond, cash/cashier's check deposit, or other required documents
return application rejected as insufficient or incomplete
triggers.clock_starts: date of original notice or rejection

rules.verbatim_quote: (2) The applicant for an original license, after having been notified to do so, fails to pay the initial license fee within 90 days from the date of the notice. (3) The applicant, after having been notified to do so, fails to file within 90 days from the date of the notice any bond or lawful money or cashier’s check deposited

verification.note: Initial fee, bond/deposit/documents, and rejected-application return each 90 days from the stated notice; withdrawal and denial are void events.

rules.title: Void date extendable up to 90 days, or one free exam reschedule, for emergencies
rules.plain_english: If a medical emergency or other circumstance beyond the applicant's control caused a missed step or exam, and it is documented, CSLB may extend the void date by up to 90 days or let the applicant reschedule one exam without a fee.
rules.verbatim_quote: The void date on an application may be extended up to 90 days or one examination may be rescheduled without a fee upon documented evidence by the applicant that the failure to complete the application process or to appear for an examination was due to a medical emergency or other circumstance beyond the control of the applicant.
rules.notes: Extension and free reschedule are alternatives ('or').

verification.note: Up to 90 days or one free reschedule, on documented medical emergency or other circumstance beyond control.

rules.title: Display the license at the main office; show proof on demand
rules.plain_english: The license certificate must be displayed at the licensee's main office or chief place of business, and the licensee must show proof of a current license and renewal on request.

parameters.display_location: main office or chief place of business

rules.verbatim_quote: The license shall be displayed in the licensee’s main office or chief place of business. Satisfactory evidence of the possession of a license and the current renewal thereof shall be provided by the licensee upon demand.

rules.title: Licenses cannot be transferred, sold or loaned
rules.plain_english: No license of any type or classification can be transferred to another person or entity under any circumstances. Buying a company does not carry over its license unless a reissuance rule below applies.
rules.applies_to: All licensees; buyers of contracting businesses
rules.verbatim_quote: No license, regardless of type or classification, shall be transferable to any other person or entity under any circumstances.

rules.title: When a license number can be reissued or moved to a new entity
rules.plain_english: A canceled, revoked, suspended or long-expired license number can be reissued to the same individual, to the same partnership with unchanged partners, or to the same corporation or LLC with unchanged Secretary of State status. It can move to a new entity for parent/subsidiary mergers, domestic/foreign conversions, a family member or family-formed company continuing a deceased or absent licensee's business, a corporation or LLC in which the individual licensee holds more than 50% of the voting power, or an LLC formed by a corporation with the same personnel.

reissue_same_holder: partnership with no change in partners or structure
corporation with no change in SOS status
LLC with no change in SOS status
reassign_new_entity: corporation/LLC: parent merged or created subsidiary, subsidiary merged into parent, or domestic/foreign filing change, continuing the business
individual immediate family member of deceased or absent individual licensee
corporation/LLC created by immediate family to continue deceased or absent individual licensee's business
corporation/LLC formed by individual licensee holding >50% of voting power directly or indirectly
LLC formed by corporation to continue its business after corporate license cancellation, same personnel

rules.applies_to: Licensees restructuring, converting to a corporation or LLC, or continuing a family business
rules.verbatim_quote: To a corporation or limited liability company when the corporation or limited liability company is formed by an individual licensee and the individual licensee maintains ownership directly or indirectly of shares or membership interests evidencing more than 50 percent of the voting power.
rules.notes: Reissuance after expiration applies only beyond the renewal period in B&P 7141 (outside this chunk).

verification.note: Reissue and reassignment conditions, 'more than 50 percent of the voting power', and the 13-member immediate-family list match. SB 800 effective 1/1/2018 confirmed.

rules.title: Sole owner dies: license canceled; family may request a continuance within 90 days
rules.plain_english: An individual license is canceled when the licensee dies. An immediate family member may request in writing, within 90 days of the death, a continuance to finish jobs in progress and take new work for a limited time. CSLB may require the bonds within 90 days of its notice, and the family member must get their own license to keep contracting after that.

parameters.trigger: death of individual licensee
continuance_scope: undertake new work for a reasonable time set by CSLB rule

rules.applies_to: Families of deceased sole-owner licensees; owners with jobs in progress
rules.verbatim_quote: An immediate member of the family of the deceased licensee may request a continuance of the license to complete projects in progress and undertake new work for a reasonable amount of time to be determined by rules of the board. The request for a continuance must be made in writing and received at the board’s headquarters office within 90 days after the death.
rules.notes: Continuance length is set by CSLB regulation, not stated here.

verification.note: Cancellation on death; written continuance request received at HQ within 90 days; bonds may be required within 90 days of board notice.

rules.title: General partner dies: partnership license canceled; notify CSLB and request continuance within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A partnership license is canceled when a general partner dies. The remaining partners must notify CSLB in writing within 90 days (a late notice is grounds for discipline) and may request a continuance within 90 days to finish projects and take new work for a limited time. They must get a new license to keep contracting after the continuance ends.

parameters.trigger: death of a general partner
continuance_scope: undertake new work for reasonable time

rules.verbatim_quote: A partnership license shall be canceled upon the death of a general partner. The remaining partner or partners shall notify the registrar in writing within 90 days of the death of a general partner. Failure to notify the registrar within 90 days of the death is grounds for disciplinary action.

verification.note: 90-day notice (late notice is discipline grounds) and 90-day continuance request match.

rules.title: General partner leaves or partnership dissolves: license canceled; 90-day notice
rules.plain_english: A partnership license is canceled when a general partner leaves or the partnership dissolves. Notice is due in writing within 90 days. If late, cancellation takes effect on the date CSLB receives notice, and the late notice is grounds for discipline. A continuance (requested within 90 days) covers only projects contracted before the departure; new work needs a new license.

parameters.late_notice_consequence: cancellation effective date written notice received at CSLB HQ; grounds for discipline
parameters.continuance_scope: only projects contracted for or in progress before disassociation/dissolution

rules.verbatim_quote: A partnership license shall be canceled upon the disassociation of a general partner or upon the dissolution of the partnership. The disassociating partner or the remaining partner or partners shall notify the registrar in writing within 90 days of the disassociation of a general partner or dissolution of the partnership.

verification.note: 90-day notice; late notice makes cancellation effective on HQ receipt and is discipline grounds; continuance limited to projects contracted for or in progress before the event.

rules.title: Limited partner dies or leaves: notify within 90 days; sole limited partner must be replaced within 90 days
rules.plain_english: General partners must notify CSLB in writing within 90 days when a limited partner dies or leaves. This does not affect the license unless the partnership had only one limited partner; then the license is canceled unless a new limited partner is added within 90 days. A continuance may be requested within 90 days if canceled.

parameters.replacement_needed_if: partnership license had only one limited partner
parameters.late_notice_consequence: grounds for discipline; for disassociation, effective date becomes date notice received

rules.verbatim_quote: The death of a limited partner will not affect the partnership license unless the partnership license has only one limited partner. In this case, the license will be canceled upon the death of the limited partner unless a new limited partner is added to the license within 90 days of the death.

verification.note: 90-day notice; only a sole limited partner triggers cancellation unless replaced within 90 days; late disassociation notice is effective on receipt (death has no such rule); 90-day continuance request.

rules.title: Joint venture license canceled when a member license ends or the JV dissolves; 90-day notice
rules.plain_english: A joint venture license is canceled if any member entity's license is canceled, revoked or disassociated, or the JV dissolves. CSLB must be notified in writing within 90 days. Late notice makes cancellation effective on receipt and is grounds for discipline. Remaining members may request a continuance within 90 days, but only to finish existing projects.

triggers: cancellation, revocation, or disassociation of any member entity license
parameters.late_notice_consequence: cancellation effective date written notice received; grounds for discipline
parameters.continuance_scope: projects contracted for or in progress before disassociation/dissolution

rules.verbatim_quote: A joint venture license shall be canceled upon the cancellation, revocation, or disassociation of any of its entity licenses or upon the dissolution of the joint venture. The registrar shall be notified in writing within 90 days of the disassociation of a joint venture entity or dissolution of the joint venture.
rules.notes: A JV license depends on every member license staying active; track all of them.

verification.note: Cancellation triggers, 90-day notice, effective-on-receipt rule, discipline grounds and 90-day continuance limited to existing projects match.

rules.title: Corporation or LLC dissolves, merges or surrenders: license canceled; notify within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A corporation or LLC license is canceled when the company dissolves, merges or surrenders its right to do business in California. The company must notify CSLB in writing within 90 days. If late, cancellation is effective when CSLB receives notice. If the company never notifies, CSLB cancels the license 60 days after it discovers the change in corporate or Secretary of State records. Late notice is grounds for discipline.

triggers: surrender of right to do business in California
parameters.late_notice_consequence: cancellation effective date written notice received; grounds for discipline

rules.applies_to: Corporation and LLC licensees (including after mergers and acquisitions)
rules.verbatim_quote: A corporation license shall be canceled upon the corporation’s dissolution, merger, or surrender of its right to do business in this state. The corporation or participating tribe shall notify the registrar in writing within 90 days of the dissolution, merger, or surrender.
rules.notes: Unlike partnerships, the text gives no continuance for corporations or LLCs. See license-number-reissue-reassignment for merger cases.

verification.note: 90-day notice; effective on receipt if late; cancellation 60 days after board discovery if never notified; discipline grounds. SB 1455 effective 1/1/2025 confirmed.

rules.title: Dispute a cancellation date within 90 days of CSLB's notice
rules.plain_english: A licensee that disputes the cancellation date may petition CSLB, showing good cause. The petition must be received within 90 days of CSLB's official cancellation notice.

parameters.trigger: date of CSLB official notice of cancellation

rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar shall review and accept the petition of a licensee who disputes the date of cancellation upon a showing of good cause. This petition shall be received within 90 days of the board’s official notice of cancellation.

verification.note: Good cause; petition received within 90 days of the board's official cancellation notice.

rules.title: Voluntary surrender cancels the license immediately with no refund
rules.plain_english: A license voluntarily surrendered is canceled as soon as CSLB receives the request, with no refund of fees. To get it back, the licensee must pay all fees and meet every requirement for an original license.

parameters.cancellation_effective: upon receipt of request by registrar
parameters.reinstatement_requires: all fees and qualifications for an original license

rules.verbatim_quote: Upon the voluntary surrender of a license by a licensee, the registrar shall order the license canceled. Cancellation will be effected upon receipt of the request by the registrar. No refund will be made of any fee which a licensee may have paid prior to the surrender of the license.
rules.notes: Inactivation (7076.5) is usually the better option if the business may resume.

rules.title: Corporation or LLC not in good standing with the Secretary of State: suspended 30 days after CSLB notice
rules.plain_english: If a corporation or LLC licensee is not registered and in good standing with the Secretary of State, CSLB sends written notice, and the license is automatically suspended 30 days later unless the company proves good standing. It can be reinstated at any time with proof.

parameters.trigger: date of CSLB written notice of SOS non-good-standing
parameters.consequence: automatic suspension by operation of law
parameters.cure: proof satisfactory to registrar of SOS registration and good standing (any time)

rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar shall notify the licensee in writing of its failure to be registered and in good standing with the Secretary of State and that the licensee shall be suspended 30 days from the date of the notice if the licensee does not provide proof satisfactory to the registrar that it is properly registered and in good standing with the Secretary of State.
rules.notes: SOS suspension often follows Franchise Tax Board issues; monitor SOS status regularly.

verification.note: Suspension 30 days from the date of the notice absent proof; reinstatement any time; tribes excluded. SB 1455 effective 1/1/2025 confirmed.

rules.title: LLC suspended for Secretary of State status: managers and officers personally liable up to $1M each
rules.plain_english: If an LLC license is suspended for not being in good standing with the Secretary of State, each person identified in B&P 7028.5 is personally liable up to $1 million each for third-party damages from licensed work done during the suspension, unless there was substantial compliance with licensing requirements.

parameters.scope: damages to third parties from any act or contract requiring a license

rules.applies_to: LLC licensees and their managers, officers and members
rules.verbatim_quote: Where the license of a limited liability company is suspended pursuant to subdivision (a), each person within the company identified in Section 7028.5 shall be personally liable up to one million dollars ($1,000,000) each for damages resulting to third parties in connection with the company’s performance, during the period of suspension, of any act or contract where a license is required
rules.notes: Who 7028.5 covers is described in an earlier section of the book, not this chunk.

verification.note: Up to $1,000,000 each for persons identified in 7028.5; third-party damages during suspension; substantial-compliance defense under 7031(e).

rules.title: Inactive license: no contracting until reactivated; valid 4 years from due date
rules.plain_english: A licensee not doing licensed work may inactivate by filing a CSLB form with its current license certificate (or a replacement fee if lost). While inactive it cannot contract until it reactivates. Inactive licenses are valid for 4 years from their due date.

to_inactivate: current active license certificate (or replacement fee if lost)

rules.verbatim_quote: The holder of an inactive license shall not be entitled to practice as a contractor until their license is reactivated. (b) Any licensed contractor who is not engaged in work or activities which require a contractor’s license may apply for an inactive license. (c) Inactive licenses shall be valid for a period of four years from their due date.
rules.notes: Contracting on an inactive license is unlicensed contracting. The 2026 amendment (SB 861) changed this section; the book does not mark which subdivisions changed.

verification.note: Extra check (numeric): inactive license valid four years from due date; no practice until reactivated.

rules.title: Inactive license: no bond, qualifier or workers' comp requirements
rules.plain_english: While a license is inactive, the contractor's bond, disciplinary bond, qualifier bond, qualifier requirement and workers' compensation requirements do not apply. A new applicant may ask for the license to be issued inactive, unless it is subject to a disciplinary bond.
rules.verbatim_quote: During the period that an existing license is inactive, no bonding requirement pursuant to Section 7071.6, 7071.8, or 7071.9, qualifier requirement pursuant to Section 7068, or workers’ compensation requirements pursuant to Section 7125 shall apply.
rules.notes: Reactivation requires restoring all of these.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 321 (B&P 7076.5(d)); PDF pages 295-296 (7071.6(c), 7071.6.5(e))
verification.note: 7071.6, 7071.8, 7071.9 bonds, 7068 qualifier and 7125 workers' comp requirements do not apply while inactive; LLC bond waived by 7071.6.5(e); issue-inactive option barred for 7071.8 applicants. SB 861 effective 1/1/2026 confirmed.

rules.title: Inactive license: renew on schedule; reactivate by paying the full active fee (no exam)
rules.plain_english: An inactive license must still be renewed on each renewal date with the inactive renewal fee. To reactivate, file an application, pay the full active renewal fee and meet all other requirements (bond, qualifier, workers' comp). No exam is needed. No refund is given for fees paid before inactivation, and CSLB may still discipline an inactive licensee.

parameters.inactive_renewal: each established renewal date with inactive renewal fee

rules.verbatim_quote: An inactive license may be reactivated by submitting an application acceptable to the registrar, by paying the full renewal fee for an active license and by fulfilling all other requirements of this chapter. No examination shall be required to reactivate an inactive license.
rules.notes: Fee amounts are in B&P 7137 (outside this chunk).

rules.title: Every original license is probationary until first renewal
rules.plain_english: Every new license (not added classifications) is probationary until its first renewal. If CSLB learns of grounds for denial, suspension or revocation during that time, it may order the licensee to show cause within 30 days why the license should not be revoked, and the license cannot be renewed while proceedings are pending.
rules.verbatim_quote: Every original license, except an additional classification issued pursuant to Section 7059, shall be a probationary license until such time as the license is renewed.

verification.note: Probationary until renewal except 7059 additional classifications; show cause within not more than 30 days; no renewal while proceedings pending.

rules.title: Report any change to license record information within 90 days
rules.plain_english: Licensees must notify CSLB in writing on its form within 90 days of any change to their recorded information, including business address, personnel, business name, qualifier bond exemption or multiple-license exemption. If late, the change takes effect only on the date CSLB receives notice, and the late notice is grounds for discipline.

parameters.trigger: date of change
parameters.late_consequence: change effective date notice received at CSLB HQ; grounds for disciplinary action

rules.verbatim_quote: licensees shall notify the registrar, on a form prescribed by the registrar, in writing within 90 days of any change to information recorded under this chapter. This notification requirement shall include, but not be limited to, changes in business address, personnel, business name, qualifying individual bond exemption pursuant to Section 7071.9,
rules.notes: Good candidate for a change-tracking reminder.

verification.note: 90-day written notice on registrar form; five listed change types; late change effective on HQ receipt; discipline grounds. AB 181 effective 1/1/2016 confirmed.

rules.title: Expired, suspended or canceled licensees must keep their address current for 5 years
rules.plain_english: A licensee whose license is expired or suspended (but renewable) or canceled must report address changes in writing within 90 days and keep a current address of record for 5 years after the license expires or is canceled.
rules.verbatim_quote: A licensee whose license is expired or suspended, and is renewable under Section 7141, or whose license is canceled, shall notify the registrar in writing of a change of address of record within 90 days, and shall maintain a current address of record during the five-year period immediately following the expiration or cancellation of the license.

verification.note: Address change within 90 days; current address for five years after expiration or cancellation. Amended effective 1/1/2008 confirmed.

rules.title: Report a valid email address at application and renewal; CSLB email is presumed delivered
rules.plain_english: Applicants must give CSLB their email address (if they have one) when applying, and licensees and registrants must give it at renewal. The email is not a public record. Email CSLB sends to that address is presumed delivered, so monitor it.

parameters.valid_email_definition: address at which person currently receives email when the application, registration or renewal is submitted

rules.applies_to: All applicants, registrants and licensees with email
rules.verbatim_quote: An applicant for licensure or registration that has a valid email address shall report to the board that email address at the time of application. (b) A registrant or licensee that has a valid email address shall report that email address to the board at the time of renewal.
rules.notes: Because of the delivery presumption, a CSLB notice sent by email may be treated as received when sent, which could start deadlines that run from 'notice'. This is an inference; the text does not say so directly.

rules.title: CSLB arbitration (optional) for complaints with damages over the bond amount and under $50,000
rules.plain_english: After investigating a complaint involving certain violations (B&P 7107, 7109, 7110, 7113, 7119, 7120) or any construction contract dispute, CSLB may send it to arbitration if both sides agree and the damages are 'material', meaning more than the $25,000 bond amount but less than $50,000. Other conditions: arbitration serves the public better than discipline, the licensee was in good standing with no history of similar violations or pending discipline, the parties have no private arbitration agreement, and they were advised of Civil Code 2855. The arbitrator's award is treated as a CSLB order.

covered_violations: any complaint arising from a contract involving works of improvement
conditions: arbitration better serves public interest than discipline
no history of repeated or similar violations
licensee in good standing at time of violation

rules.applies_to: Licensees and owners/consumers with CSLB complaints
rules.verbatim_quote: For the purposes of paragraph (1), “material damages” means damages greater than the amount of the bond required under subdivision (a) of Section 7071.6, but less than fifty thousand dollars ($50,000).
rules.notes: The $25,000 lower bound is the current 7071.6(a) bond amount; it moves if the bond amount changes. A contract with a private arbitration clause takes the dispute out of this program.

verification.note: 'material damages' = greater than the 7071.6(a) bond amount ($25,000) but less than $50,000; concurrence of both parties; seven findings; award deemed registrar's order.

rules.title: CSLB arbitration is mandatory when damages or contract price are at or below the bond amount
rules.plain_english: When a possible violation exists and the contract price or the damages claimed are at or below the bond amount ($25,000), CSLB must refer the complaint to arbitration if the public-interest, good-standing, no-history, no-pending-discipline and no-private-arbitration conditions are met. The licensee's consent is not required.

parameters.measure: contract price or demand for damages

rules.applies_to: Licensees and owners/consumers with smaller CSLB complaints
rules.verbatim_quote: In all cases in which a possible violation of the sections set forth in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) exists and the contract price, or the demand for damages is equal to or less than the amount of the bond required under Section 7071.6, but, regardless of the contract price, the complaint shall be referred to arbitration,
rules.notes: The printed text looks garbled or incomplete ('but, regardless of the contract price,' runs straight into 'the complaint shall be referred'); the official statute likely limits the demand for damages to the bond amount regardless of contract price. Verify against the official code before coding this threshold.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 325 (B&P 7085(b)); PDF page 326 (B&P 7085.4(b))
verification.note: Quote matches the law book exactly, including the awkward 'but, regardless of the contract price,' clause; mandatory referral using criteria (2)-(6); 7085.4(b) confirms the licensee's failure to return the notice does not stop referral. The note's guess about the codified wording could not be checked (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov is not reachable from this session); the law book prints it this way.

rules.title: Return the CSLB arbitration agreement or notice within 30 calendar days
rules.plain_english: Once CSLB offers arbitration, both parties must return the 'agreement to arbitrate' (optional cases) or the 'notice to arbitrate' (mandatory cases) within 30 calendar days of the mailing date. In mandatory cases, a complainant who does not return it has the complaint closed, but a licensee who does not return it can still be sent to arbitration and bound by an enforceable award.

parameters.trigger: date CSLB mails the agreement or notice
parameters.licensee_failure_mandatory_case: arbitration and award enforcement may proceed anyway
parties_informed_of: consequences of administrative arbitration vs judicial remedies
right to retain counsel at own expense

rules.applies_to: Licensees and complainants in CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: This agreement shall be returned to the registrar within 30 calendar days of the date that the agreement is mailed by the registrar. The return of this agreement by the parties shall authorize the registrar to proceed with administrative arbitration.
rules.notes: Calendar days, not business days.

verification.note: 30 calendar days from mailing for both the agreement and the notice; complainant non-return closes the complaint; licensee non-return does not bar referral or enforcement.

rules.title: Strike and rank the arbitrator list within 7 days or accept all names
rules.plain_english: In CSLB arbitration, each party gets the same list of possible arbitrators and has 7 days from the mailing date to cross off objectionable names, rank the rest and return it. If a party does not return the list in time, every name on it is treated as acceptable. CSLB pays the arbitration fee from the Contractors License Fund.

parameters.trigger: mailing date of arbitrator list
agreement_must_include: names, addresses, phone numbers of parties
amount in dollars or other remedy sought

rules.applies_to: Licensees and complainants in CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: Each party to the dispute shall have seven days from the mailing date in which to cross off any names to which it objects, number the remaining names to indicate the order of preference, and return the list to the board or appointed arbitration association. If a party does not return the list within the time specified, all persons named in the list are acceptable.
rules.notes: The chunk ends partway through 7085.5(b)(1); the remaining arbitration rules are in the next chunk.

verification.note: Seven days from mailing; unreturned list means all names acceptable; fee paid from the Contractors License Fund; agreement contents match. The 7085.5 history note falls outside this chunk, so 'effective' is left blank.

verification_summary.method: Every target rule (deadline, money_amount, threshold, penalty, required_notice; this file has no required_contract_clause rules) was read against the full section text in sources/lawbook.txt, where PDF page N is the Nth form-feed page (pages 268-328 read). Every verbatim_quote was string-matched against the cited pages after removing running headers and line-break hyphens; all target quotes match. Numbers, triggers, comparisons, exceptions and effective dates were checked against the section text and history notes. Six non-target rules with numeric parameters were also checked. leginfo.legislature.ca.gov was not reachable, so no outside source was used.
